Title: Property Editor
Content: Objective Edit selected item's properties in the Property Editor. Operation Property Editor Pattern Property Shows a patterns property on the Property Editor when it is selected Internal Shape Property Shows an internal shapes property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Sewing Property Shows a sewing line's property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Stitch Property Shows a stitch's property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Fabric Property Shows a patterns property on the Property Editor when it is selected from the fabric list. Button Property Shows a buttons property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Buttonhole Property Shows a buttonholes property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Avatar Property Shows the pattern-related properties of an avatar on the Property Editor when it is selected. Simulation Property Shows the simulation properties on the Property Editor. Right click on the 3D Pattern Window and select Simulation Property from the pop-up menu. Wind Property Shows the wind properties on the Property Editor. Right click on the 3D Pattern Window and select Wind Property from the pop-up menu. 2D Window Property Shows the 2D Pattern Window properties on the Property Editor. Right click on the 2D Pattern Window and select 2D Pattern Window Property from the pop-up menu. Simulation Property Follow and select the menu as below. Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Simulation Properties Open, save, and edit properties related to Simulation in the Property Editor. Note: Select All with Same Property: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Patterns) Select All with Same Property Particle Distance/ Layer/ Fabric Patterns with the same property is selected.

Title: Object Browser
Content: Objective View and edit items used in both 3D and 2D Windows such as Scene, Fabric, Button, Buttonhole, Topstitch, and Puckering. Operation Note: Show or hide the Object Browser by clicking Main Menu Display Window Object Browser (Show) Scene Scene tab is the primary, fastest, and most streamlined tool for finding or selecting object. It lets you quickly review a list of all objects and its structure in the 3D and 2D Windows. The list is in the order of object created, but when you click on Name, the object list is sorted A to Z (1 to 10). Once you click again, the list is reordered and sorted Z to A (10 to 1). Fabric Fabric Tab represents the menu for Fabric. Users can select, add, copy and reset Fabric. Click and drag to reorder Fabric styles as desired (ver4.1.0). Button Button Tab displays a list of button items. User can select, add, and copy Button. Buttonhole Buttonhole Tab displays a list of Buttonhole items. Users can select, add, and copy Buttonholes Topstitch Topstitch Tab displays a list of Topstitch items. Users can select, add, and copy Topstitch. Note: Merge to new Fabric/Button/Buttonhole/Topstitch (Above ver. 11) - Select multiple items Right-click the mouse on the selected Left-click on the Merge to new Fabric/Button/Buttonhole/Topstitch to merge the selected items into a new Default Item

Title: 2D Window
Content: Objective The 2D Window is a 2D area where it is possible to design patterns, set seamlines, and edit fabric textures. Operation Note: Show or hide the 2D Window by clicking on Main Menu Window 2D Pattern Window.

Title: 3D Window
Content: Objective 3D Window is a 3D area where it is possible to simulate garments and move avatars to create animations. Operation Note: Show or hide the 3D Window by clicking on Main Menu Windows 3D Window

Title: Menu
Content: The Main Menu is located on the topmost left of the Marvelous Designer, and a pop-up menu can be launched by right clicking in the 3D Window View and the 2D Window View for fast access to each function. 3D Background Pop-up Menu Avatar Pop-up Menu Pattern Pop-up Menu 3D Window View 2D Background Pop-up Menu Pattern Pop-up Menu Line/Point Pop-up Menu Seawing Pop-up Menu Topology Pop-up Menu Texture Pop-up Menu Topstitch Pop-up Menu 2D Window View Main Menu Located on the topmost left of the Marvelous Designer, it shows the menus for each function.

Title: History Window
Content: Objective Keep track of your workflow with the History window and revert to previous points at any given time. In addition, save 3D states to review and compare specific points of progress. Location 3D State History Window 3D State Delete &amp Rename Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) Delete or Rename Operation 3D State Follow the indicated guideline below: History Window 3D State Double click the desired 3D State. Warning as follows appears: "Loading the 3D State will delete the current History. Would you like to proceed?" Select OK. The 3D garment is reverted to the selected 3D State. Delete &amp Rename Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) Delete or Rename The name field is highlighted and name can be changed. The selected 3D State is deleted. You can find a preview window if hovering your mouse over the thumbnail of a desired '3D State' file. (ver. 12.2)

Title: Mode
Content: Objective Marvelous Designer provides total of five Mode as follows: Simulation, Animation, Modular, UV Editor and Sculpt Mode. Location Switch between Mode using the button on the right-top corner of the window. Operation Simulation Mode is a mode where it is possible to create and edit patterns in the 2D Window or animate draping of Garments, Poses, or Actions in the 3D Window. Animation Mode is a mode where it is possible to record, play and edit Garment animations. Modular Mode is a mode where it is possible to mix and match Garment components, such as sleeves and collars, as blocks to test and create new styles. UV Editor Mode is a mode where editing UV of Garment. (Ver. MD 7.5) Sculpt Mode Sculpt garments using various brush tools. (ver. MD8)

Title: Trace
Content: Objective Use the Trace function to convert lines/shapes/area to Patterns. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Operation Trace as a Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Select the Baselines to be traced. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as a Pattern. The selected Baselines are traced as a Pattern. Trace as an Internal Shape Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Select the Baselines to be traced. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as an Internal Shape. When the selected lines are intersected, the intersection is joined and the lines are traced as one shape. Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Select the Baselines to be traced. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes. The selected lines will be traced as they are. Note: To easily select a closed shape, double click on the Internal Line. Click and drag to select multiple Internal Lines at once. All Internal Lines within the marquee box are selected.

Title: Spiral
Content: Objective Create a Spiral pattern in the 2D Pattern Window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Spiral 2D Pattern Window Toolbar Create Pattern Shape Dropdown Menu Spiral Operation Select the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". Click in the 2D Pattern Window. The Create Spiral pop-up Window appears. After setting the options below, click OK. Radius Set the radius at which a spiral pattern rotates. Length Set the length of the Inner/Outer segment of the spiral pattern. (the two values are linked - editing one will automatically adjust the other) Side Set the Inside/Outside width of the spiral pattern's ends. (editing either will automatically adjust the Length values slightly) Offset Adjust the spacing between spirals. The length you enter is the distance from the center of the spiral pattern to the center of the next spiral layer. Direction Set the rotation direction (Clockwise/Counterclockwise) of the spiral pattern. A spiral pattern is created.

Title: Create AI Bezier Curve
Content: Objective Create curves in Marvelous Designer similarly how they are drawn in Adobe Illustrator (ver3.0.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line Operation Create AI Curves Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line Click and drag on the 2D window. The curve is created as the blue handle appears. Continue to drag to adjust curvature. When the desired curvature is achieved, let go the mouse cursor. To draw a straight line or change the direction of the curve, click on the point created at last. Then, continue to draw polygon or Internal Polygon/Line. Cancel Actions To cancel all actions, hit Esc key or Ctrl + Z keys on the keyboard. All the actions taken to create polygon or Internal Polygon/Line are undone. To cancel the last step, hit Delete key or Backspace key on the keyboard. The point created at last is undone.

Title: Segment Darts
Content: Objective Add or modify Darts located along Pattern outlines. Location Create Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) Add Dart Edit Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) Edit Dart Operation Create Choose the Edit pattern (Z) tool from the 2D toolbar and click on the point which a Dart should be added. The clicked point is selected and highlighted in yellow. Follow the indicated guideline below. Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) Add Dart The Dart window appears. Adjust the below options as needed and click OK. Name Description Total Width Set the total horizontal length of a Dart. Dart Arm Width Set 1/2 of the horizontal length of a Dart. Length Set the depth of a Dart. The Dart is created based on the above settings. Edit Choose the Edit pattern (Z) tool from the 2D toolbar and select Pattern outlines that form the Dart. The segments are selected and highlighted in yellow. Follow the indicated guideline below. Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) Edit Dart The Dart window appears. Similarly, adjust the options in the Dart window and select OK. Any modified settings are reflected on the Dart.

Title: Dart
Content: Objective Create darts inside Patterns. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Dart 2D Toolbar Dart Operation Create Dart Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Dart 2D Toolbar Dart Click and drag within the Pattern to create a Dart. Release the mouse to complete the Dart. Create Dart with Dimension and Position Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Dart 2D Toolbar Dart Click once within the Pattern. The Create Dart window appears. Enter the desired values for following options. Dimension Enter the desired values for Width (Left,) Width (Right,) Height (Up,) Height (Down.) All values are measured from the center of the Dart. Position Outline Designate the Dart's position within the Pattern by entering the margin between the Dart outline and the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Center Designate the Dart's position within the Pattern by entering the distance between the center of the Dart and the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Note: Internal Shape Tool Group

Title: Rectangle
Content: Objective Create rectangle Patterns in 2D window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Rectangle 2D Toolbar Rectangle Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Rectangle 2D Toolbar Rectangle Click and drag the left mouse button in the 2D window. Release the mouse button to create a rectangle Pattern. Note: While creating the Pattern, press down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a square Pattern (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Pattern, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Pattern, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a square Pattern by its center point (ver.5.1.0). Click on the 2D window to open the Create Rectangle window. Here, a rectangle Pattern can be created with the desired width and height values. If Width and Height are linked while entering the values, the ratio is fixed. If the link is canceled, the ratio can be set according to user's preference. Note: Create Pattern Tool Group

Title: Create Multiple Patterns or Internal Shapes and Input Intervals
Content: Objective Designate the number of shapes and input the interval when creating Patterns or Internal Lines. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Applicable Tools 2D Toolbar Applicable Tools Note: Applicable tools are as follows: Rectangle tool, Internal Rectangle tool, Ellipse tool, Internal Ellipse tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline as below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Applicable Tool 2D Toolbar Applicable Tools Click once on the 2D window. The pop-up window with options to create the selected Pattern or Internal Shape appears. Enter desired values for options below the Replicate category and click OK. Name Description Number of Shapes Set the number of replicated shapes. Interval Set the distance between each Pattern or Internal Shape/Line. Angle Set the direction that the replicated Patterns are placed. The Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines are replicated based on the settings.

Title: Internal Polygon/Line
Content: Objective Create Internal Polygons and Lines inside a Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar Internal Polygon/Line Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar Internal Polygon/Line Click within a Pattern to establish the start point of an Internal Polygon/Line. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand the Internal Polygon/Line. Right click while freehanding the Internal Polygon/Line to access the Create Internal Polygon/Line window. Use Length, Mirror Creation, and Position options to create the Internal Polygon/Line more precisely and conveniently. Option Description Length Length Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) Mirror Creating The Internal Polygon/Line is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis Local Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. Position Left Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its left. Right Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its right. Top Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its top. Bottom Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its bottom. To complete an Internal Polygon, click the start point. On the other hand, to complete an Internal Line, double click the last point. Note: Right click inside a Pattern to open the Create Internal Polygon window and type in desired values. An Internal Polygon is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). Click inside a Pattern to create the start point of an Internal Line. Then, drag and right click to open the Create Internal Polygon window. Enter desired values. An Internal Line is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). Hold down the Ctrl key as creating an Internal Polygon/Line to create curves. Hold down the Shift key to drag the mouse in straight lines or in 45º diagonal lines. Note: Internal Shape Tool Group Note: Mirror Creating

Title: Internal Ellipse
Content: Objective Create internal ellipses or circles within Patterns. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar Internal Ellipse Operation Create Internal Ellipse Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar Internal Ellipse Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an ellipse. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Ellipse or the Internal Circle. Note: While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). Create Internal Ellipse with Entered Values Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar Internal Ellipse Click once within a Pattern. The Create Ellipse window appears. Enter the desired values. Diameter Set the diameter of the Internal Circle. Radius Set the radius of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). Link to maintain the width and height ratio. Circumference Set the circumference of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). Position To Outline Set the position of the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Circles from the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). To Center Set the position of the center of the Internal Circle from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Note: Internal Shape Tool Group

Title: Internal Rectangle Tool
Content: Objective Create a rectangle inside a Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Rectangle 2D Toolbar Internal Rectangle Operation Create Internal Rectangle Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Rectangle 2D Toolbar Internal Rectangle Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an Internal Rectangle. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Rectangle. Note: While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a square (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a square Internal Shape by its center point (ver.5.1.0). Create Internal Rectangle with Measurement Input Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Rectangle 2D Toolbar Internal Rectangle Click once within a Pattern. The Create Rectangle window appears. Enter appropriate values in the options indicated below. Width Set width of an Internal Rectangle. Height Set height of an Internal Rectangle. Link width and height to adjust them in a fixed ratio. Position Outline Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the outline of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0). Center Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the center of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0). Note: Internal Shape Tool Group

Title: Ellipse
Content: Objective Create ellipse or circle Patterns in the 2D window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Ellipse 2D Toolbar Ellipse Operation Create Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Ellipse 2D Toolbar Ellipse Click and drag on the 2D window. A preview of an ellipse appears. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. While creating the Pattern, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Pattern, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). Release the mouse when the desired shape is achieved. The ellipse Pattern is created. Create with Specific Values Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Ellipse 2D Toolbar Ellipse Click in the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. Type in the desired values for the options below. Diameter Set the diameter of the circle Pattern. Radius Set the radius of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). Link to maintain the width and height ratio. Circumference Set the circumference of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). Note: Create Pattern Tool Group

Title: Polygon
Content: Objective Create polygon Patterns in 2D Window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Polygon 2D Toolbar Polygon Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Polygon 2D Toolbar Polygon Click on the 2D window to make the start point. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand a polygon. Right click while freehanding a polygon. The Create Polygon window appears. Length or Mirror Creation options to create polygon more precisely and conveniently. Option Description Length Length Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) Mirror Creation The polygon is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis Local Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. Click again on the start point to complete the polygon. Note: Pressing the keyboards Delete key while setting points to create a pattern cancels the points, starting from the most recent one. Furthermore, pressing the Esc/Ctrl+Z key during creation cancels the entire operation. While making points to create a Pattern, holding down the Ctrl key and setting points turns segment points into Free Curve Points. This creates a polygon Pattern made up of curved lines. Setting a Segment Point while holding down shift reveals a guideline that can move horizontally, vertically, and diagonally at a 45 degree angle according to the Segment Point. Note: Create Pattern Tool Group Note: Mirror Creating

Title: [Library] 18 default MetaHuman body types supported (ver 2024.0.173)
Content: 18 default MetaHuman body types supported (ver 2024.0.173) Select a desired MetaHuman body type and create an outfit for your MetaHuman in Marvelous Designer before bringing the outfit to Unreal Engine as USD files Steps You can find the MetaHuman body types and download it from the library. Location Library Click Avatar Folder MetaHuman Double click to download a desired MetaHuman body types End Result The MetaHuman body will appear in the 3D window based on the selected files you chose.

Title: Avatar Properties (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Set the avatar's properties. When you select an avatar, its properties appear in the property window. Avatar Properties Properties Description Information Name Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. Model You can change the type of avatar. Surface Skin Offset Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. Static Friction The friction when a garment is in stationary position. Kinetic Friction The friction when a garment is moving. Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0) Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. Note: When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. Soft Body Stiffness Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. Material (Selected) Set the Material of the avatar. Miscellaneous Mesh Type Indicates the type of avatar mesh. Element Count Indicates the number of points in the mesh. Smooth Avatar Smooth Toggles the Smooth option on or off. If the option is on, the mesh on the avatar's surface will be divided as set in 'Division Level'. Division Level Can be split by a factor of 1 to 5. Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0)

Title: Auto Convert to Avatar (Ver. 2024.0)
Content: Auto Convert to Avatar (Ver. 2024.0) Automatically converts externally created avatars into default avatar types in Marvelous Designer. Automatically convert your custom avatar into a compatible avatar of matching default internal skeleton and motions. Steps Run it along the path below. Location Main menu Avatar Auto Convert to Avatar Please refer to the table below and automatically convert it into the avatar of Marvelous Designer. Basic Original File - Import the desired avatar file format (OBJ, AVT, FBX, or FBX - DAZ Genesis Avatar) (Ver. 2024.1) NOTE: This tool is recommended to be used with Human shaped Avatar Mesh in an A-pose. Gender - You can select the option of the desired gender. - The format is as follows: Female Male Girl (7-20) Boy (7-20) Kid (2-6) Baby (6-18m) DAZ Avatar's gender will automatically populate (Ver. 2024.1) Converting option Automatic Automatically converts the avatar's body shape. Custom (Maintain current rig) The body shape is converted while maintaining the joint positions of the original avatar file. Exclude hands and feet: When the "Exclude Hands and Feet option" is selected, the Marvelous Designer avatar's hands and feet will be retained when transforming the avatar's body shape. Converted Type MD Skin Style Keep the body shape of the original avatar file and convert only the appearance to a Marvelous Designer Avatar and add joint points. Rigging Only Maintains the body shape and appearance of the original avatar file, only adding articulation points. Size Editable Change the default avatar body shape and add articulation points in the Marvelous Designer to allow for size editing while preserving the shape of the file to be converted. Save Path File Name(AVT) Name the avatar you want to save as an AVT file. File path Specify the path of the file you want to save. End Result The Avatars will appear in the 3D window based on the selected options chosen.

Title: [Property] Scale Avatars
Content: Objective Scale an OBJ imported as an Avatar. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Import an .OBJ as an Avatar. (ver. 10) Import a .FBX as an Avatar. (ver. 2024.0) Select the tool/ menu indicated in Location. Select the Avatar and click the Scale button to resize the Avatar. The scale Gizmo appears. Click and drag the Gizmo's X-axis (red), Y-axis (yellow-green), Z-axis (blue) or the rectangle. The Avatar size is adjusted according to the selected direction. Click the Scale button to complete scaling. The Gizmo is changed to a standard one that is used to move or rotate the Avatar. Note: Scale with specific values in the Property Window after selecting the Avatar.

Title: [Size Editor] Adjust Avatar Size (ver. 10)
Content: Objective Create an avatar with your own measurements. As Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Avatar Size Operation Load an Avatar (.avt). Only the avatars provided in ver. 10 V2 and above can be adjusted. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Avatar Size Measures appear on the Avatar. The editable measures appear in black, whereas the non-editable measures appear in grey. Refer to below graph and adjust the Avatar as needed. Option Description Select Avatar Select the Avatar to be edited. This option only appears when two or more Avatars are in the 3D window. Total Body Shape the overall body type with Avatar's height and chest width. In order to get realistic shapes for body parts without assignable measurements, use the Total Body option to create an overall shape and then insert measurements under the Details option. Height Assign Avatar's height. Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Degree of Accuracy based on Height Measure Standard: HPS Height &gt Inseam &gt Total Height Total Height Insert the height measured from the ground to the head. Note: It is more accurate to assign height with either HPS Height or Inseam option as individual has different head length. The Total Height option is not recommended as it has the lowest accuracy. HPS Height Insert the height measured from the ground to the neck. Inseam Insert the height measured from the ground to the crotch. Width Select and insert desired value as the standard of the overall body width Details Configure Avatar's detailed measurements. Due to a technical reason, a small error may be generated even after inserting a specific measure. The error appears in parentheses next to each measurement and the real measurement can be checked with the measure appears on the Avatar. Edit the Avatar based on the measure appears on the Avatar as the numbers appear in the Avatar Editor only shows the measurements assigned by users. Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Each measurement can be checked with the measure that appears on the Avatar. Basic Use the Basic option when only a small amount of body measurements are available. Unassigned body parts are automatically adjusted based on the real body scan data and the measurements inserted by the user. Advanced Use the Advanced option when available body measurements are abundant. When all measurements under the Advanced options are not available, please use the Basic option to create more realistic body as unassigned measurements are fixed with the default values pre-assigned to each option. Show All Measurements/ Show Editable Measurements By default, only editable measurements appear in the window. To view all measurements, click the Show All Measurements icon. * Use the Save button to save the adjusted measurements and use the Open button to reload. However, any measurements created with lower versions are not compatible.

Title: Avatar Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Set the Zipper or Slider via the right-click pop-up menu. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the avatar. The pop-up menu appears. Avatar Options Menu Descriptions Select All Faces Select and modify all surfaces of an Avatar. Delete Avatar Select an avatar and delete it individually. Delete All Avatars Delete the entire avatar. Delete Scene and Prop Delete the selected Scene and Prop. (ver. 2024.0) Delete All Scene and Props Delete the entire Scene and Prop. Move Avatar/ Move All Avatars &amp Garments Move Avatar or all Avatars and garments to the center of the 3D window or the ground. Reset Joints Reset joints of the Avatars. Change Heels (ver MD10) Make Avatars' heels up or down. Deactivate/Activate Avatar Deactivate or activate avatars as needed. When it is deactivated, the garments do not recognize while simulation. Hide Avatar Show or hide individual avatar. Show/Hide All Avatars Show or hide all avatars. Refresh Textures Refresh the textures of the avatar. Export to USD Layer Export as USD Layer.

Title: Default Avatar Download Link
Content: Click links below to download default avatar files (FBX file format). Male_A Female_A Kid_A Kid_B Kid_C

Title: Adjust Avatar Location
Content: Objective Adjust avatar location by using its X-Ray joint points. Location Main Menu Display Avatar Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Avatar Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) Select purple point (pelvis point) in the middle of the avatar. Click and drag or move it with the Gizmo to relocate the avatar.

Title: Play Motion
Content: Objective Play Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) files. Location Main Menu Avatar Play Motion 2D Toolbar Play Motion Operation Pose Open a Pose file. When a Pose file is loaded, the Play Motion tool is automatically activated. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Play Motion 2D Toolbar Play Motion Click the Play Motion tool while the Avatar changes pose. The Avatar stops temporarily. The Avatar changes pose again. Motion Open a Motion file. The Play Motion tool now can be selected. Click the Play Motion tool. The motion is played. * The Transition Animation for the default avatars of the version 10 is not compatible with the previous versions.

Title: Morph Target with AVT Files
Content: Objective Apply morph target function onto the AVT files to change the avatar Pose or shape. Location Main Menu File Open Avatar Main Menu File Add Avatar Operation Open an Avatar in the 3D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Avatar Main Menu File Add Avatar The Add Avatar or Open Avatar window appears. Select Load as Morph Target for the Load Type and select OK. If morphing succeeds, the first avatar Pose or shape changes to the second avatar Pose or shape. If morphing fails, a warning pop-up window appears and no change is made.

Title: Change Pose by Collada's Joint Information
Content: Objective Note: Only available for file formats with avatar joint information. In this case, COLLADA is being used. As the avatar's joints move when the pose changes, it is possible to change the avatar's pose while keeping the simulation stable even if there is a large difference between the starting and ending poses. However, if the avatar is exported via DAZ Studio, some composition form information may be lost during the process. Therefore, it is necessary to load the posed avatar's OBJ file and adjust the garments after changing the pose. (The avatar's OBJ file only saves the composition form information, so there is no danger of losing information during the loading process.) Operation Export a T-pose avatar which can be easily draped and an avatar with the final pose in COLLADA files. To find out export methods from DAZ Studio and Poser in details, check 3D File (COLLADA) Import for the reference. After exporting the COLLADA files, export the avatar poses in OBJ files. Load a posed COLLADA file from the previously saved avatars in program. Click File Save Pose to save current avatar as POS file. After dressing T-pose avatar, this file is going to be used when changing current pose. Click File Open Avatar to open the previously saved T-pose COLLADA file. Dress the avatar with desired garments. Now Click File Open Pose to open the previously saved POS file. The avatar slowly changes poses. It may take a while depending on the complexity of the garments. After the pose changes, load an OBJ file without any loss and adjust garments. Click File Import OBJ to open the previously saved final pose OBJ file. Highly positive to observe garments being under the avatar's surface. While simulation is being activated, drag out the parts of the garment that are located under the surface of the avatar by using the left mouse button. To find more details in Select/Move tool, check Move Garment for the reference.
